_note: Source capture queue and capture log. Each queue entry names the document that must be obtained and the exact question it must answer. test/capture-manifest.test.js fails if an entry is contradicted by the repository — a city that reaches Grade A while still listed here, or an entry whose blocking question has quietly disappeared. The manifest is not a wish list; it is the part of the Index that is honest about not existing yet. It records what was obtained and when, and states nothing about grades, rules or what currently holds a city: those are computed from the tariff records and the acceptance gate, so a withdrawn rule cannot survive here as a stale sentence.

queue.utility: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks

documents_required.what: A designation of the ordinary residential bore, or a statement of which bore a single dwelling in the 23 wards is connected on
documents_required.answers: §2.5, and it is what holds the supply metric at Grade B. The ordinance prices twelve bores and the ready-reckoner three; neither designates one. 20 mm is taken from the Bureau's own residential worked example, which is documented suitability rather than designation.

documents_required.what: The Bureau of Sewerage's own rate schedule for the 23 wards
documents_required.answers: Nothing that is currently open. The sewerage structure is read from the waterworks ready-reckoner and reconciled at two volumes that fix both band boundaries. This would move the figure from the collecting utility's table to the levying authority's schedule, which is tidier provenance for the same numbers.

known_traps: The payable price of 55 yen/m3 and the structural 140.80 yen/m3 differ by a factor of 2.56. Publishing one without the other is a citation trap, and the site now carries both with the payable named as the headline.
The waiver runs May-August OR June-September by meter-read cycle. A single monthly payable figure hides that.
The first 5 m3 a month is a basic volume inside the basic charge, not a free tier. Under the waiver the charge goes to zero and the allowance survives.
A city under live relief is out of the UWTI base basket under §5.4, whatever its grade.
The issuer calls the measure limited to this summer and has now run it two years running. Record what the issuer says; note the repetition; do not reclassify it as structural.

The measure amends no charging article and is paid for out of the metropolitan general account. That is what makes the structural price the tariff rather than a reconstruction of a suspended one — and it is a fact about this waiver, not a general rule about relief.
The rate tables date from 2005 (water) and 1998 (sewerage); what changed in December 2019 was the tax multiplier. Do not report the tariff as having been set in 2019.
The guidance page's FAQ prints collapsed. Ten questions are captured and no answer is. Anything sourced to that FAQ is sourced to a question.
queue.queue_status: Queued only for two documents that would improve provenance without moving a figure: a designation of the ordinary residential bore, which holds the supply metric at Grade B under §2.5, and the Bureau of Sewerage's own schedule, which would move the sewerage rate from the collecting utility's table to the levying authority's. Both metrics are published. The waiver instrument was obtained on 18 August 2026.

documents_required.what: law.go.kr 부가가치세법 제26조 obtained by hand, or a Seoul Metropolitan Government statement on 하수도 사용료
documents_required.answers: the total water services metric. Art. 26(1)2 names 수돗물 and not sewerage; a sewerage use charge is levied by a local authority under the Sewerage Act rather than supplied by a business, which is a different question from exemption.

documents_required.what: A primary designation of the ordinary residential connection size
documents_required.answers: §2.5, and it is what keeps the supply metric at Grade B. Arisu prices eight bores and designates none as ordinary for a single dwelling, so 15 mm is the smallest priced rather than the designated one.

known_traps: Do not close the tax question with the silence of the rate table. That argument worked for Hong Kong's fixed charge because WSD enumerated everything a bill can carry; a rate table enumerates rates only.

Arisu's own page contradicts itself: the prose describes a three-band progressive structure for all four categories while the table shows domestic as a single rate and dates itself to July 2021. The table governs.
Apartments on a shared meter have the basic charge apportioned between households. That is a different reference customer from a separately metered dwelling.
The published sewerage schedule runs to 2030. A future rate is not an observation and must not be published as one.
queue.queue_status: Supply metric published. Queued only for the sewerage tax treatment and a designated connection size.

queue.utility: TAQA Distribution (formerly Abu Dhabi Distribution Company)

documents_required.what: Whether a residential wastewater charge is levied on a metered Abu Dhabi household, by whom and at what rate
documents_required.answers: Total Water Services, and nothing else now. TAQA Distribution's own tariff document prices no wastewater tariff for any segment while the bill guide lists Waste Water among the services a bill can show. Either a standardizable rate or a demonstrated absence closes it. The supply metric no longer depends on this: the separate bill line is what shows AED 7.84 to be water alone.

documents_required.what: Any Executive Council or Department of Energy instrument setting or superseding the residential water tariff since 1 January 2025
documents_required.answers: Whether continuity rests on the publisher's schedule or on a recorded search over the instruments themselves. Currently the former, which Rule 3.10 permits for a live schedule.

known_traps: A tariff booklet that prices one fixed charge proves it can carry fixed charges. It does not prove it lists everything a bill can carry, and confirmed_absent needs the second. Hong Kong's fixed-charge absence was closed because WSD enumerated every item a bill may contain; the equivalent document here is the bill guide, not the tariff booklet. Booking this to the booklet alone repeats the Seoul error in the opposite direction.
A calculator is not the schedule. The AED 150 unmetered figure is admissible from the tariff booklet and not from the calculator that also displays it.

ADDC and TAQA Distribution are the same publisher under two names. Each source record must state the name under which that capture was published, or the lineage from 2017 to the valuation date will look like three publishers agreeing when it is one publisher repeating itself.
Continued validity is a claim about the absence of a superseding instrument. Not having found one is not the same as having looked; the search has to be recorded with the finding.

AED 7.84 appears twice in Abu Dhabi with different meanings: the water rate per cubic metre, and a monthly electricity meter service charge in secondary sources. Do not let one stand in for the other.
The residency split is elective and applies to one property per UAE National. §5.3: the benchmark uses the general non-concessionary class and never averages.
The Green allowance is daily. Applying 0.7 m³ to a monthly volume overstates the bill by more than 20%.
Do not borrow Dubai's conventions. The meter multiplication factor of 220 is DEWA's.
The VAT question was closed by an unchanged rate across the introduction of the tax, not by preferring one ADDC page over another. The superseded reading — AED 117.60 — stays visible in the record.

A tariff booklet that prices one fixed charge proves it can carry fixed charges. It does not prove it lists everything a bill can carry, and confirmed_absent needs the second. The bill guide is the enumeration; the booklet is not.

The guide's specimen bill is a UAE National account at AED 2.090 and 2.600. It establishes the format and the arithmetic of a residential water bill and not the price of the benchmark one. Reading the concessionary rate off it would be §5.3 broken by the very document that closed §7.6.
queue.queue_status: Queued only for the services metric and for tidier continuity. The supply figure is published at Grade A: the Understand Your Bill guide arrived on 18 August 2026 and closed the recurring-charge question by enumeration and arithmetic together.

documents_required.what: The tariff schedule for residential water and sewerage as published by the issuing authority
documents_required.answers: the first-band reading and the meter service charge. The four-block structure and the SAR 5/month charge for 0-20 mm circulate widely and are not captured from an instrument.
documents_required.where: Start at the National Water Company, https://www.nwc.com.sa/EN/Pages/default.aspx, and at the Saudi Water Authority, https://www.swa.gov.sa/en/related-sectors/nwc. Note the institutional change: this queue entry names the Water and Electricity Regulatory Authority, and the sector body now appearing is the Saudi Water Authority. Which one issues the current tariff should be established before the annex is cited. Calculator sites attribute the restructuring to WERA regulatory decision 1/26 of 1438H; that attribution is discovery under 7.1 and the decision itself has not been seen.

documents_required.what: A regulated or NWC primary source on VAT applied to residential water usage, to sewerage, and to the meter service charge separately
documents_required.answers: THE BLOCKER. The generic 15% Saudi rate must not be applied automatically to three components that may be treated differently. Every secondary source found on 19 August 2026 does exactly that — states 15% on the total — which is the assumption this component exists to refuse, restated rather than evidenced.
documents_required.where: ZATCA publishes sector guidelines as PDFs under https://zatca.gov.sa/en/HelpCenter/guidelines/ ; confirmed examples of the path are .../Documents/Input%20Tax%20Deduction.pdf and .../Documents/Guideline-on-Imports-and-Exports-under-VAT-Provision.pdf . No guideline specific to water or utilities was found on 19 August 2026. A dated NWC tax invoice showing the VAT line against each component would also close it, on the Abu Dhabi and Toronto pattern: an enumerated bill answers this better than a reading of a general rate does.

documents_required.what: Whether the reference account is sewer-connected, and on what basis
documents_required.answers: the services figure. Sewerage is 50% of the corresponding water rate but connection is account-dependent.

known_traps: At SAR 6.50 a month this will be the cheapest bill in the Index by an order of magnitude. Rule 13 forbids calling it cheap or efficient: a low bill measures what the household pays, not what the water costs to produce.

search_log.result: No admissible source found. Results were calculators, price aggregators and news, plus IB-NET's tariff database entry at https://tariffs.ib-net.org/sites/IBNET/ViewTariff?tariffId=1436 which points at a third-party PDF. Each restates the four blocks, the 50% sewerage rule and 15% VAT without an instrument behind any of them. Riyadh holds zero archived sources: this is a city to be built, not a document to be chased.

documents_required.what: The same national annex as Riyadh, plus confirmation that Jeddah is served under it
documents_required.answers: whether one tariff function serves two city records

known_traps: Two Saudi cities cannot both enter the UWTI base basket: freezeBase() refuses more than one territory per country. Create both records; mark one basket-eligible at most.

documents_required.what: A designation of the ordinary residential meter diameter, or a statement of how a collectively metered building is billed
documents_required.answers: Grade A on the supply metric, and the arrangement most Parisians live under. Fourteen diameters are priced and none is named; 15 mm is used as the smallest priced. Neither question holds a figure.

known_traps: 15 x 4.23 = €63.45 is a Total Water Services figure and not a TWJ Water Supply Bill. Publishing it as the latter would be the Toronto error with extra steps.
Until decomposed, Paris is Grade C on the supply metric and its published total is quotable only as what it is.

The VAT rate sorts the lines: 5.5% is drinking water, 10% is collective sanitation, and the rates are statutory. That is what makes the split a decomposition rather than an allocation — do not present it as a judgement call.
Six of the seven drinking-water lines are levies rather than the supply rate. Quoting Fourniture d'eau potable alone as the Paris water price understates it by a third.

The catalogue is dated in its own footer as 'Catalogue 2024 - Version adoptee (12/2023)'. The column headings and every figure are 2026; the footer is a stale template artefact and is not the document's date.
queue.queue_status: Closed as a blocker on 19 August 2026. The Catalogue des tarifs 2026 was captured and the published 4,23 EUR/m3 decomposes into ten volumetric lines summing to 4,2300 exactly. Both metrics publish at Grade B; what remains is the §2.5 designation and a scope question about collective metering.
queue.spec_note: Not an expansion fixture. Paris went from queue to published record in one step, because the document that was blocking it turned out to contain the whole decomposition; the tariff record is the spec.

documents_required.answers: the Domestic Full consumption bands and the meter-size fixed charge. Nothing is computed until this is read from the primary document

documents_required.what: The Tariffs, Fees and Charges Book for the same period
documents_required.answers: cross-checks the above and carries the fixed charges

documents_required.what: The basis of the 15% VAT stated by the City's own calculator
documents_required.answers: whether the 15% VAT applies to the volumetric steps, to the fixed charge, and to sanitation separately. The City's calculator states it uses 15%; a calculator is not the schedule.

known_traps: Cape Town has a stepped domestic tariff and a separate indigent tariff. §5.3: the benchmark uses the general non-concessionary class.
Do not take figures from secondary articles. This city in particular attracts them.

queue.queue_status: Queued for provenance and for a decision, not for a blocker. The tax component closed on 19 August 2026 and Total Water Services is published at Grade A. The supply metric is a structural exception under Rule 5.1 and is not waiting for a document at all.

documents_required.what: The current version of Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 441, Appendix D, Schedule 1
documents_required.answers: Whether the 2026 rate in the by-law is 4.8629 or 4.8630. The captured version is dated 11 February 2025 and gives C$4.6872; Council approved 3.75% from 1 January 2026, and 4.6872 x 1.0375 = 4.862970, which rounds to 4.8630 and truncates to 4.8629. The City's live rates page now prints 4.8629, which settles what the rate is and not how it was rounded — and the statutory schedule is what the record would roll to. Not a blocker: the 2025 observation is closed with a date and nothing published moves until somebody moves it.

documents_required.what: The Excise Tax Act provision behind the absent tax on a combined municipal water and wastewater charge
documents_required.answers: Why no tax is charged, which the bill shows but does not explain. Provenance rather than a figure: the City's worked bill closes on its two service charges, and that is what a household pays. The statutory route is not obvious, because relief for unbottled water supplied by a municipality and relief for wastewater services are separate questions with separate answers. Look in Schedule V, Part VI.

known_traps: Do not accept 4.8629 from a secondary source because it agrees with the City's rounded total of C$1,118 at 230 m3. That total constrains the rate only to roughly 4.860-4.865.

Schedule 3 Ref 2 prices a sewer surcharge on private water at 57% of Block 1, which invites a 43/57 decomposition into C$2.0155 supply. Refused under Rule 3.3 and recorded in the tariff as a refused inference. Do not revive it.
The 2026 rates were approved as INTERIM and may be amended when the rate-supported budgets are considered. An interim rate is a different observation from a final one.

The absence of a tax line and the absence of a mention are different evidence. A schedule that names HST against one fee and not another is suggestive; a worked bill whose total closes on its service charges is arithmetic. Do not cite the first as if it were the second.
The City prints two rates, on-or-before and after due date, and the difference is the early payment discount. Applying the discount to the on-or-before rate counts it twice.
